subject: Sandbox-to-Prod SDK Migration: sprint plan + token backoff & quota-smoothing
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Aiden Chen <aiden@orchidpay.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@orchidpay.com>
Date: 2028-10-21T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sandbox-to-Prod SDK Migration: sprint plan + token backoff & quota-smoothing

Hi Aiden / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, I put together a compact sprint plan to move OrchidPay from sandbox traffic to a staged production cutover with minimal risk. The focus areas are: SDK bootstrap, endpoint migration, graceful token backoff, and short-term quota smoothing during ramp.

High-level proposal (attached spreadsheet has dates):
- Week 1 (Sandbox hardening): dependency checks, enable telemetry, run smoke tests against sandbox endpoints.
- Week 2 (Canary rollout): 5% of traffic to dedicated sandbox canary using the SDK gateway; enable prefix caching.
- Week 3 (Staggered cutover): increase to 25/50/100% with automated rollback thresholds.

Key operational levers I recommend we implement before canary:
- Client token backoff strategy (exponential with jitter, see token-backoff-snippets.md).
- Per-token rate smoothing on the SDK side to avoid global quota spikes.
- Short TTL caching for repeated prompt prefixes (saves tokens during ramp).

Next steps: I’ll loop in Vanessa (implementation coordinator) and Soojin (runtime ops) to draft the runbook and sample snippets. Can you confirm the target production cutover week (we tentatively set 2028-11-06) and whether you want a single-day cutover or staggered across endpoints?

Rafael Mendes
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
rafel@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0121

Attachment stubs: orchid-multi-env-plan.xlsx, raf-sdk-bootstrap-samples.zip, token-backoff-snippets.md
From: Aiden Chen <aiden@orchidpay.com>

Date: 2028-10-21T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sandbox-to-Prod SDK Migration: sprint plan + token backoff & quota-smoothing

Thanks Rafael — this looks good and concise. Quick answers:
- Cutover week: yes, 2028-11-06 still works for us.
- Prefer staggered approach by endpoint (payments-ui first, then reconciliation).
- We have an internal rate limiter that currently rejects on 429s; would like the SDK to handle smoothing to avoid huge bursts.

Couple of asks before we start Week 1:
1) Sample code for client-side token backoff that we can drop into our JS SDK and Go backend.
2) A checklist for telemetry events we should enable to validate quality during canary (latency, token usage per request, 429s).

Priya — any legal/procurement checks needed before Week 2?

—Aiden
Senior Platform Engineer, OrchidPay

Subject: Re: Sandbox-to-Prod SDK Migration: sprint plan + token backoff & quota-smoothing

Hi all —

Attaching the runtime checklist and three sample snippets: JS exponential backoff with jitter, Go retry wrapper with token-aware backpressure header, and a server-side rate-smoothing helper that uses a leaky-bucket to limit bursts. High-level notes in the attached token-backoff-snippets.md.

Telemetry checklist (short):
- request.latency_ms (p50/p95)
- token.count_per_request
- response.429_count and response.5xx_count
- cache.hit_rate (prefix cache)
- request.kv_cache_size

Operational thresholds I recommend we enforce in the canary automation:
- If p95 latency increases >2x baseline for >10 minutes => auto rollback.
- If 429 rate exceeds 1% of total requests for 5m => pause ramp and enable quota bump.

I will spin up a test harness in sandbox that runs a 10-minute synthetic traffic profile and verify the leaky-bucket keeps tail spikes <15% of baseline.

—Soojin
Runtime Ops, Redwood Inference
